_comment: Optional software for Labyrinth. Everything not listed here is the base system. Used by /usr/local/bin/labyrinth-apps on an installed system and by scripts/gen-packages.py when building an ISO. Package names marked unverified were not found in Arch's repos (CachyOS repo or AUR). enable_global: user services enabled for every user (systemctl --global); enable_system: system services (systemctl enable --now).

components.name: Steam and Proton
components.description: Steam, Valve's Proton (ships inside Steam), Proton-CachyOS, ProtonUp-Qt, Protontricks, umu, Wine, GameMode, MangoHud, 32-bit NVIDIA, AMD and Vulkan libraries.
components.notes: Start Steam once and sign in, then run: labyrinth-gaming setup

components.name: Spotify
components.description: Arch's spotify-launcher, which downloads Spotify's own Linux client on first run. Spotify says its Linux client is not officially supported. The bar's media controls talk to it over MPRIS.
components.notes: Run spotify-launcher once to download the client, then sign in.

components.name: Obsidian
components.description: Notes app, from Arch's official repo. Proprietary but free for personal use. Do not run Obsidian Sync and a cloud-folder sync on the same vault.

components.name: Visual Studio Code
components.description: Microsoft's official VS Code build (their Linux tarball, repackaged and pinned with its published SHA-256), with the Microsoft extension marketplace. Microsoft's own Linux instructions cover Debian, Fedora, Snap and a community AUR package. Arch's repo has `code`, the open-source build, which uses the Open VSX marketplace and lacks Microsoft-only extensions; it conflicts with this one.
components.notes: Built on this machine with makepkg. Updating means changing the pinned version in its PKGBUILD.

components.name: Weather (forecast and rain alerts)
components.description: Labyrinth's weather engine: GFS, ECMWF and ICON models plus a 30-member ensemble, with an honest uncertainty range, scored against measured airport temperatures over time, and a rain nowcast for the next two hours (Open-Meteo's 15-minute data). The temperature sits in the top bar with "rain in 20 min" when a shower is coming, and one notification arrives before it. Uses Open-Meteo and aviationweather.gov, which receive the coordinates of your place. The place comes from your time zone until you choose Automatic (nearby Wi-Fi network IDs and your IP address go to beaconDB, an open non-profit database) or search for one.
components.notes: Works right away for your time zone's main city. For your exact place, open the Weather card in the top bar, press Settings and choose Automatic (nearby Wi-Fi, through beaconDB) or search for a place.

components.name: Proton Drive (rclone)
components.description: rclone with FUSE, to mount Proton Drive at ~/ProtonDrive and to link and verify folders with minos-cloud. No official Proton Drive client exists for Linux.
components.notes: One-time: run `rclone config`, create a remote named proton of type protondrive. Minos's Cloud > Proton Drive signs in and starts the mount (the proton-drive user unit comes with Minos).

components.name: Proton Pass
components.description: Proton's official desktop app, repackaged from their RPM and pinned to one version with its published SHA-512. Built on this machine with makepkg.
components.notes: The browser extension installs from your browser's store.

components.name: Proton VPN
components.description: Proton's official Linux VPN app (GTK) and its split-tunnelling daemon, from Arch's extra repository. Needs a Proton account. Keeps its login in the system keyring (gnome-keyring, already part of Labyrinth).
components.notes: Open Proton VPN from the start menu and sign in. Split tunnelling needs systemd-resolved (not enabled by default: `sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved`, which changes how DNS is set up). Proton says Arch support is community-maintained. Apps set to Ask or Block in Settings > Apps still follow those rules inside the tunnel.

components.name: Screen reader and speech
components.description: Orca (screen reader), Speech Dispatcher with eSpeak NG (the voice), and Braille support (brltty). Settings, Minos and the admin password box expose themselves to screen readers; the top bar, dock, start menu and lock screen do not yet (see docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md).
components.notes: Start Orca with Super+Alt+S (or `orca` in a terminal). It reads what programs tell the accessibility bus (AT-SPI).

components.name: Creative apps
components.description: Krita, Darktable (photo), OBS Studio (video), Ardour (music).

components.name: Virtual machines (Limbo)
components.description: QEMU, libvirt, UEFI firmware, dnsmasq and nftables, which Limbo uses to run sandboxed guests.

components.name: Reverse engineering (REA and Ghidra, sandboxed)
components.description: REA (MIT, an MCP/CLI for reverse engineering) with the NSA's Ghidra, run by labyrinth-rea inside a bubblewrap sandbox (no network, no home, read-only files), for Sarina's reverse_engineer tool and for you. Static analysis only; analysing, not running, drivers, firmware and suspicious files.
components.notes: Then run labyrinth-rea-setup once (downloads REA from npm, pinned, and Ghidra from GitHub with its hash checked; about 700 MB). Put files to examine in ~/Documents/Samples.

components.name: Limbo (sandboxed apps and VMs)
components.description: Limbo runs Windows and Linux guest apps as sandboxed windows with a firewall per guest, quarantine and reports. Built here with makepkg from the Limbo repository; needs the Virtual machines component for its runtime.
components.notes: Check what is missing with: limbo doctor. Then: sudo limbo plan or up with a manifest (examples are in /usr/share/doc/limbo-git/examples). Windows guests need your own Windows ISO and license.

components.name: Local AI runtime
components.description: Ollama, the model server Sarina uses: ollama-cuda on NVIDIA (about 6 GB with CUDA), ollama-vulkan otherwise. Not in the image; Sarina offers to install it the first time it is needed. Models compete with games for GPU memory.

components.name: Fedora / Debian containers (Distrobox)
components.description: Podman and Distrobox: run a Fedora, Debian or Ubuntu userland inside your desktop, with its apps appearing in the app menu, sharing your home folder. For software that only ships .rpm or .deb. Create one with: distrobox create --name fedora --image fedora:latest --nvidia
components.notes: Containers share the host kernel and, with --nvidia, the GPU driver. Not tested here.

components.name: Flatpak
components.description: Flatpak, the distro-neutral app format used by Flathub. Many apps that list only Fedora or Debian also publish there.
components.notes: Add the store once: flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo

components.name: Sarina (local AI agent)
components.description: Sarina, the local-model agent: a Go program that talks to any OpenAI-compatible model server (such as Ollama), calls tools, and keeps sessions on disk. Built here with makepkg from the Sarina repository.
components.notes: Needs a model server. Install Ollama (the local-ai component, or the plain 'ollama' package on a machine without an NVIDIA card), pull a model, then: sarina chat --interactive. The web console is 'sarina gui'.

components.name: Daedalus CAD
components.description: Daedalus CAD, a SketchUp-style modeler in Rust: 3D push/pull modeling, a solid inspector and sheet-metal flat patterns (DXF with cut and bend layers). Built here with makepkg from the Daedalus_CAD repository.
components.notes: Early software: push/pull, undo and the inspector work; many tools are still planned. Opens STL, OBJ, DXF and DAE.

components.name: Heimdall (security agent for Sarina)
components.description: Heimdall, a separate program that watches what Sarina writes to disk for prompt injection, leaked credentials, invisible-Unicode smuggling and permission escalation. Built here with makepkg from the Heimdall repository. Installed but not started.
components.notes: Not enabled by default. Copy /etc/heimdall/config.json.example to config.json, set what it watches, then: sudo systemctl enable --now heimdall.

components.name: Developer tools
components.description: What Claude Code and most command-line development want on the PATH: Node.js and npm (MCP servers run with npx), jq, the GitHub CLI, pip, and bubblewrap and socat (Claude Code's sandbox). Git itself is in the base system.
components.notes: Claude Code itself is installed per user: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash (see docs/CLAUDE_CODE.md)

components.name: ASUS laptop and tablet tools
components.description: asusctl and ROG Control Center: fan and power profiles, keyboard lighting, battery charge limit on ASUS laptops and tablets (ROG, TUF, Zenbook, ROG Flow). The installer already keeps them on ASUS computers.
components.notes: Open ROG Control Center from the start menu.

components.name: CoolerControl
components.description: Fan curves and pump speeds for AIO coolers and fan controllers (Corsair Commander and iCUE coolers, NZXT, Lian Li, EK and many motherboards), driven by the temperatures you pick. Uses liquidctl underneath.
components.notes: Open CoolerControl, pick a device and draw its curve. The settings are kept by the coolercontrold service and apply from start-up, without the app open.

components.name: OpenRGB
components.description: One app for RGB lighting across makers: Corsair, Razer, ASUS Aura, MSI, Gigabyte, G.Skill memory, and many keyboards, mice and fans.
components.notes: Some motherboard and memory lighting needs the i2c modules; OpenRGB explains it when a device is missing.

components.name: Corsair keyboards and mice (ckb-next)
components.description: Lighting, macros and key remapping for Corsair keyboards and mice, the iCUE part for peripherals.
components.notes: Open ckb-next; the device appears once the daemon is running.

components.name: Razer keyboards and mice
components.description: OpenRazer (the driver) with Polychromatic for lighting, DPI and polling rate, and Input Remapper for the extra mouse buttons: give any button a key, a shortcut or a macro.
components.notes: Log out and in once after installing (the openrazer group). Polychromatic sets lighting; Input Remapper sets the buttons.

components.name: Android apps (Waydroid)
components.description: Runs Android apps in their own windows next to your other apps: a full Android system in a container, sharing the kernel (no emulator, near-native speed). The Android image (about 1 GB) is downloaded from Waydroid's servers when it is set up.
components.notes: Start 'Waydroid' from the start menu; the first start takes a minute. Install Android apps from an APK (waydroid app install FILE.apk) or an open store such as F-Droid. Google Play needs the image with Google apps: sudo waydroid init -s GAPPS -f. If Android has no internet, the firewall is blocking it: sudo ufw allow in on waydroid0 && sudo ufw route allow in on waydroid0.

components.name: Agent usage (bar add-on)
components.description: Claude's weekly and 5-hour limits in Yggdrasil's top bar, red when the week's use is ahead of an even pace. Built here with makepkg from Yggdrasil's repository (needs Rust once, to build).
components.notes: Shows nothing until Claude Code is signed in on this account. The numbers come from Anthropic, asked with Claude Code's own sign-in.

components.name: Authenticator (Proton Authenticator codes)
components.description: Proton's official Authenticator app (from the AUR, Proton's own release) and Yggdrasil's Authenticator window: search your 2FA codes and copy one with Enter. The window reads the app's local vault read-only through devSviat's pa-helper; nothing goes over the network.
components.notes: Open Proton Authenticator once, sign in and let it sync; then the Authenticator window shows your codes.

components.name: Timer (top bar)
components.description: Countdown timers in Yggdrasil's top bar: click the pill for presets (1 to 60 minutes), your own time and a label, pause and +1 minute; several can run at once. The alarm is a systemd user timer, so nothing runs while it counts, and it rings even with the window closed. Built here with makepkg from Yggdrasil's repository (needs Rust once, to build).
components.notes: From a terminal or a shortcut: yggdrasil-timer start 25m Tea.

components.name: Health Mode (reminders)
components.description: Gentle reminders to rest your eyes (20-20-20), move, drink water and breathe, plus a meal and a wind-down reminder at set times. Nothing is sent while you are away or the screen is locked, quiet hours and pause are a click away, and the top bar counts down to the next one. Built here with makepkg from Yggdrasil's repository (needs Rust once, to build).
components.notes: Click the heart in the top bar to choose reminders and intervals.

components.name: Browser warm start
components.description: Keeps your default browser started in the background with no window, so a new window opens at once instead of after half a second or more. Chromium-family browsers only (Chromium, Brave, Vivaldi, Chrome, Edge); Firefox has no such mode. Costs about 0.5 to 0.8 GB of memory. A browser you set to run sandboxed is never started this way, and after an update it is restarted only when it has no windows open. Built here with makepkg from Yggdrasil's repository (needs Rust once, to build).
components.notes: Quitting the browser from its menu starts it again in the background within a minute; remove the plugin to stop that.
